thread:
Olivia S.: heads up — multiple support tickets reporting SSE streams dropping mid-response from eu-west-1. Customers see partial output (hang at ~40-60% tokens) then stream closes. ~15 incidents in last 30m, several urgent (>p1) from fintech customers.

Matt B.: thx. any correlation with model or route? which models are involved?

Olivia S.: mostly gpt-4o-ish endpoints and the redwood/generic-13b variants. routes: /v1/streams/generate and /v1/streams/chat. customers report reconnects with 1006 websocket-like close codes (client-side).

Ashley K.: pulling runtime logs now. seeing a spike of 502/timeout from our sse-proxy in eu-west-1 for streaming connections. KC cache reports look ok. forwarding relevant log snippet.

Ashley K.: ```
2026-03-15T09:12:23Z sse-proxy[eus-01] connection_id=xyz status=502 reason="upstream read timeout" model=redwood/generic-13b seq=42
2026-03-15T09:12:24Z sse-proxy[eus-02] connection_id=abc status=502 reason="connection reset by peer" model=gpt-4o-16k
```

Tim R.: hmm latency to model-serving nodes also increased ~2x in the same window per perf-dashboard. Could be autoscaler thrash or a kernel OOM from recent quantization tweak. rolling back the quant patch on eu-serving group.

Matt B.: good call. I'm going to fail traffic for streaming in eu-west-1 to fallback region (us-east-1) for affected customers. We'll preserve non-streaming API (polling) in eu-west for now.

Priya - Support Lead: need a short status update for the customers in the queue. Can you confirm expected ETA for failover? Also flag any billing or auth implications.

Matt B.: failover plan: update smart-routing policy to route streaming requests from eu-west-1 to us-east-1 for the tenant list we have in the P1 tickets. ETA ~8-12m to change routing and let edge caches expire. No billing changes — usage routes to a different region but charges as usual. Auth unaffected (tokens are global).

Olivia S.: drafting message: "We're failing streaming requests to a healthy fallback region while we investigate — you'll see a short increase in cold-start latency. No data loss expected. More updates in 30m." Any additions? :speech_balloon:

Tim R.: add: "If you rely on VPC-only routing in eu-west, contact support — we will not failover those customers without approval"

Ashley K.: we've applied the rollback on a subset of serving nodes — preliminary logs show reduced 502s but still some residual resets. I'm pushing a full rollback now.

incident-bot: /status set: "partial streaming outages eu-west-1 — failing streaming to us-east-1 for affected tenants. Investigating root cause."

Olivia S.: posted customer message and pinged the top 10 affected accounts. got a thumbs-up from two customers who are ok with the fallback.

Matt B.: routing change is live for the tenant subset. observability: streaming success rate in eu-west should drop (expected) and appear in us-east success metrics. watching for any auth anomalies.

support-bot: ticket #45217 updated: "Streams failing — routed to fallback region, ETA 12m".

Olivia S.: several customers reporting reconnects are now getting complete responses but with ~300-800ms higher end-to-end latency. one customer (acme-pay) still sees partial outputs.

Ashley K.: looking into acme-pay's specific requests — their client uses very long-lived connections with ping disabled. I see our proxy dropping idle connections after 60s when upstream stalls; we'll temporarily increase proxy idle timeout to 180s for eu-west streaming pool.

Matt B.: applied proxy timeout increase for the pool. also instructed autoscaler to add 2 warm replicas to reduce cold-starts.

Tim R.: after full rollback + proxy timeout bump, error rate dropped to baseline in the past 7m for non-long-lived clients. acme-pay test now completes end-to-end — they confirm success.

Priya - Support Lead: great. compose final customer note: "Issue mitigated — streaming requests were routed to a fallback region and proxy timeout was adjusted. We rolled back a recent serving change that correlated with the failures. We'll follow up with a root cause within 72 hours and any required credits."

Olivia S.: sent update to all affected customers. two customers requested credits; flagged for CS to review.

Matt B.: next steps: 1) deep dive on quantization patch interaction with network stack (assigned to Ashley), 2) add canary for streaming traffic on config changes, 3) update runbook to include safe-proxy-timeout gating, 4) automate failover for tenant classes. I'll create follow-up tickets.

Ashley K.: opening ticket ENG-9931 (quant-patch root cause), attaching heap/dmesg + perf traces.

incident-bot: /incident close: "mitigated — partial streaming outages eu-west-1" (initial postmortem scheduled).

Olivia S.: closing thread for now. thanks everyone for the quick turnaround. will file postmortem notes once we have the RCA. :pray:
